Rollout readiness

Readiness evidence for an installed gateway release.

About 4 min read

Run gateway rollout after each machine installs the published archive. It is a read-only gate: it does not restart the service, acquire a gateway generation, or reconnect a desktop client.

gateway rollout
gateway rollout --json
gateway rollout --verify

ready means all of the following agree on one installed release. Since 1.5.8 two processes may keep an older release label, by design of the no-restart move, and are reported as versions.retained: the service root that wrote the status, only while its live controller (runtime.controllerRelease) already runs the installed release (any other service root stays pending), and the native relay, only while its binary is byte-identical to the one the installed release ships (every current release reuses an earlier relay, 1.5.9 as of 1.7.1). Both change at the next natural start. A desktop adapter whose release ships the installed release's gateway SDK is retained too: it waits for its app's next launch rather than exiting under it (services). Everything below still has to be current, including the execution host and its canary. A live-moved service whose host still runs the older release and refuses chats of the installed one is blocked: release_skew.

  1. Each relevant loaded gateway process has a known immutable release and it matches the installed release.
  2. The service status belongs to the currently running service PID, has a fresh frozen runningRelease, and its running plan components are current.
  3. The local inference health endpoint answers HTTP 200 with the installed X-Gateway-Release header. A successful body alone is insufficient.
  4. The execution host belongs to that service PID and OS start stamp, attests its immutable release source, active catalog fingerprint, verified SDK, and direct-tool compatibility.
  5. The host's fresh canary proves a completed turn with a direct tool edit and Git commit. Its proof must name the same host, SDK, source, and active catalog fingerprint.

A pending Claude consolidation cannot earn ready, even when the old service's canary passes. A normal pending receipt waits until every legacy Claude job is unloaded; an idle socket snapshot does not make an automatic cutover safe. A receipt explicitly staged with gateway service claude-desktop --on-restart --force may interrupt its exact owned jobs and must be treated as a maintenance-window cutover, not normal automatic migration. The gate checks the staged receipt before and after verification. Once adopted, each Claude component must have its own running PID, matching OS start and expected executable. Its deliberately pinned private JavaScript is not relabeled as the main installed release; its authenticated endpoints require separate post-migration checks.

On Linux, external component executable identity comes from /proc/<pid>/exe after the PID, owner and start stamp match. It does not require lsof; unreadable or mismatched executable identity keeps the component pending.

The normal command accepts only a host-controlled cached canary report that is less than five minutes old and still matches the live status. --verify runs a new isolated serving-host canary. It uses a local mock provider and a temporary repository; it does not use an account, send provider inference, replay chats, or write user gateway state.

State Exit Meaning
ready 0 All required live evidence agrees.
pending 1 A process, service, host, or proof has not adopted the release yet. Recheck after idle adoption.
blocked 1 The host explicitly reports active work, so a canary was not claimed.
blocked (release_skew) 1 The service still runs an older release and the host refused chats of the installed release since the service last moved or started, so chats do not open. A lagging adapter or listener alone stays process_version_pending. Forwarding should have prevented it; finish turns or run gateway service restart --interrupt. A live controller swap does not count as a move.
failed 2 Inference or the direct-tool canary failed. Investigate before publishing or declaring the machine ready.

The command reports only fixed reason codes, counts, versions, capabilities and PIDs. It does not print command lines, paths, request bodies, tool arguments, configuration values, or probe-child output.

A pending native-sharing intent keeps the rollout pending even when its gateway tool canary passes. After combined adoption, the host must also hold the actual native-home lease; advertising the native capability alone is insufficient. The current canary requires gateway sharing. A native-only service uses its service status and the shared-native fixture instead of this combined gate.

A live supervisor controller reports runtime.controllerRelease independently from its root's runningRelease. Controller adoption does not change the bootstrap process version or attest the retained host and relay. Those components remain pending in this gate until their own evidence agrees with the installed release; a controller swap must never be relabeled as full rollout readiness.
